Description: Research theme focused on building computational or mathematical models to simulate, predict, or explain biological/cancer-related processes.
Research theme focused on developing software tools, databases, or computational infrastructure for the cancer research community.
Mechanisms, functions, activities, or processes exhibited by tumors or pathogens to withstand previously toxic drugs.
Notes: interpretive/partial: NCIT 'Drug Resistance Process' covers only the resistance half of this compound theme

Description: Topic concerning the study of heritable changes, for example in gene expression or phenotype, caused by mechanisms other than changes in the DNA sequence.
The process by which organism populations change over successive generations that is influenced by gene mutation and natural selection.
Research theme focused on creating or characterizing new experimental (wet-lab) model systems, such as cell lines, organoids, or animal models.
The quality or state of consisting of elements that are not of the same kind or nature.
Therapy designed to induce changes in a patient's immune status in order to treat disease.
Research theme focused on how mechanical forces influence gene expression and genetic regulation within cells and tissues.
Research theme focused on how mechanical properties of cells or tissues contribute to resistance against therapies or disease progression.
Organic processes in a cell or organism that are necessary to sustain life, encompassing both anabolism (construction of complex molecules) and catabolism (breakdown of complex substances).
Notes: interpretive: no exact 'Metabolism' label in NCIT; mapped to 'Metabolic Process'

Description: The spread or migration of cancer cells from one part of the body (the organ in which it first appeared) to another. The secondary tumor contains cells that are like those in the original (primary) tumor.
Research theme focused on creating or improving experimental methods, assays, or protocols.

The cellular and molecular environment immediately surrounding a tumor, including blood vessels, immune cells, fibroblasts, signaling molecules, and extracellular matrix, that interacts with and influences tumor growth and progression.
Notes: interpretive: NCIT term is 'Tumor Microenvironment' - no bare 'Microenvironment' concept in NCIT; accepted given cancer-research grant context

Description: Research theme focused on cellular stress responses induced by oncogenic events, such as DNA damage response or replication stress.
Research theme focused on developing new experimental or technological platforms for cancer research.
A pathologic process in which alterations at the molecular level result in a more aggressive cytologic and phenotypic profile and clinical course of a neoplasm.
Interactions of the immune system and tumor cells.
Notes: interpretive: mapped to NCIT 'Tumor Immunology' (closest single-concept match)
